body:
This PR records a new upper bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant (problem 21): **Λ < 319/2000 = 0.1595**, unconditionally. It changes Markdown only: a new row and reference on `constants/21a.md`, the README cell (`0.2 (0.1595*)`), and one Recent-progress line.

**Stacked on #208.** This branch contains #208's two commits (the 0.16 row) plus one commit for 0.1595, so the two PRs cannot conflict. Merging this PR alone also lands the 0.16 row; if #208 is merged first, this PR's diff reduces to the single 0.1595 commit.

**Claim.** Λ < 319/2000. The only finite-height input on the Riemann hypothesis is Platt–Trudgian 2021 [PT2021] (RH up to height 3000175332800), used only at height X/2 with X = 6000000185827, an exact margin of 350479773/2. The route is collision exclusion, as in #208: if Λ > 0, then H_Λ has a multiple real zero. The certificate shows that H_t has no multiple real zero for any t in the closed band [319/2000, 3/16] and any real x, with two modules (interior x ≤ X, exterior x ≥ X with every index N ≥ 690988 and no terminal cutoff) whose union is checked in exact arithmetic. With the existing bound Λ ≤ 3/16 ([MI2026b], the 0.1875 row) this gives Λ < 319/2000.

**How to verify.** The certificate bundle is pinned at commit [cc81078](https://github.com/463464q435q43/optimizationproblems/tree/cc8107854fedd5a96d7eb695178f405568712f35/certificates/certified01595) on our fork. Its [VERIFY.md](https://github.com/463464q435q43/optimizationproblems/blob/cc8107854fedd5a96d7eb695178f405568712f35/certificates/certified01595/VERIFY.md) gives the environment (Ubuntu 24.04 with Python 3.12, python-flint 0.9.0, sympy 1.12 and mpmath 1.2.1) and one command. The command checks `MANIFEST.sha256`, runs the official scorer, and prints `lambda_upper_exact 319/2000` with every gate 1 and 168846 checks. The bundle reproduces on a fresh machine with that command: on a fresh 6-vCPU cloud machine, installing the packages took about 11 s and the command about 3 s.

To reproduce (after VERIFY.md's environment step):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/463464q435q43/optimizationproblems.git && cd optimizationproblems
git checkout cc8107854fedd5a96d7eb695178f405568712f35 && cd certificates/certified01595
sha256sum -c --quiet MANIFEST.sha256 && python3 verify/record_score.py --candidate assembly_ce_319_2000 --out "$(mktemp -d)/score.json" --timeout 1500
```

This prints `{"ok": true, "score": 0.1595, "error": null}`. VERIFY.md's full command also prints every gate and compares the verify output byte for byte with the banked run.

**Provenance.** Found and certified by Mosaic Intelligence's verifier-gated AI agent swarm (GPT-6 Astra Pro agents). Inside the swarm, two separate harness runs (official and verify) both scored the package at 319/2000 with every gate 1, and its LLM audit review passed. Before publication an independent check re-scored the package on fresh cloud machines, including from a source-only copy, and re-ran the banked checks behind 13 of the lines it relies on; everything matched. After publication, the pinned commit was fetched from GitHub onto another fresh machine and VERIFY.md was run verbatim: 319/2000 with every gate 1, verify output byte-identical to the banked run, and all 7 products regenerated byte-identically from a source-only copy. A passing run is a mechanical check, not a referee's verdict; the analytic arguments (`assembly_ce_319_2000/ASSEMBLY.md` and `math/ASSEMBLY.md` in the bundle) are offered for review.

**AI use.** This is a fully AI-derived result: the construction, the proofs and the checkers were produced and checked by Mosaic Intelligence's automated agent system, and this text was AI-prepared.

**Acknowledgment.** The collision-exclusion approach of the open pull request #180 inspired part of this route; the certificate does not depend on it, and no file, theorem, constant or code from it is used.
